candidates.computation_change_reason: The table defines multiple parallel limit types (ambient Ca, effluent Ce, formula-derived 2.13*Ce, domestic/chronic/human-health instream concentrations, and separate Domestic/Irrigation/Livestock & Wildlife/Acute Aquatic/Chronic Aquatic/Human Health criteria columns). Different readings of which column is the operative enforceable discharge limit—or whether these are screening values rather than permit limits—would change which numeric limit is selected for comparison (A) and whether associated monitoring is tied to a limit-bearing parameter (B).

MQL is presented as a per-pollutant reporting/detection threshold. Interpreting MQL as a compliance floor, a report-only qualifier, or a basis for non-detect handling would change whether measured values below MQL can be compared to limits (A) and how missing or below-detection results are classified (C).

The acute aquatic instream limit is expressed as a function of effluent concentration (2.13*Ce). If Ce is read as zero, not measured, or not applicable, the derived limit changes accordingly, altering which numeric value—if any—is used for exceedance evaluation.

This row lists several distinct numeric criteria for the same pollutant (Domestic Criteria 1 ug/l, Chronic Aquatic 19, Acute Aquatic 15, Human Health 30) alongside 1E+100 placeholders in other columns. Which criterion is selected as the governing enforceable limit depends on interpretation of column applicability and the sentinel values.

Repeated 1E+100 entries appear across criteria columns. Reading these as non-operative placeholders, as effectively unbounded limits, or as missing data would change whether a numeric compliance comparison is applicable (A) and whether monitoring for that criterion is considered required or not applicable (B).

Unlike other pollutants on this page, Nonylphenol has no MQL value but does list Acute Aquatic (28) and Chronic Aquatic (6.6) criteria. Whether the blank MQL means no quantitation requirement, inherited default, or incomplete data affects limit/monitoring applicability (A,B) and how absent or non-detect results should be classified (C).

The Need TMDL column is present for every pollutant with values shown as N/A. Interpreting N/A as 'no TMDL-driven limit applies' versus 'TMDL status undetermined' would change whether TMDL-based limits are candidates for enforceable discharge limit selection.

This pollutant grouping label may indicate a monitoring or analyte-class condition (e.g., base/neutral extractable fraction). Different readings of whether membership in this class triggers distinct monitoring requirements would change evaluated monitoring obligations.

Representative row pattern: effluent/ambient/instream-derived columns are all 0 while Domestic Criteria (70) and Human Health Criteria (5300) are nonzero. Interpreting the zeros as documented no-discharge/no-reasonable-potential versus missing effluent data changes whether numeric limits are considered applicable (A), whether monitoring was required for the period (B), and whether absence of reported results reflects a documented no-data state or unresolved missing evidence (C).
